name: logos
description: Derive-macro lexer generator focused on speed; the de-facto companion to lalrpop/chumsky

license.comment: Cargo.toml: `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` (dual); README repeats the dual licence.

approach.comment: Lexer generator only: `#[derive(Logos)]` on a token enum with `#[token]`/`#[regex]` attributes compiles all patterns into one DFA. No parsing facilities; the book pairs it with chumsky (calculator example) and LALRPOP's book pairs it as the external lexer.

implementation.comment: Runtime crate depends only on `logos-derive`; the codegen crate's deps (fnv, proc-macro2, quote, regex-automata, regex-syntax, syn) are all pure Rust — no `cc` or C code.

documentation.comment: The Logos Handbook (mdBook); API reference at docs.rs/logos.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; published 2026-01-30. Research reflects logos 0.16.x (the 0.16 line rewrote the matching engine for full regex semantics; MSRV 1.80).

grammar-class.comment: Not applicable: logos is a lexer generator that compiles regular expressions (regex-syntax subset, no lookaround/word boundaries) into a DFA — a regular language recogniser. None of the defined grammar-class tags (LR/LALR/GLR/PEG/recursive descent/LL(k)/arbitrary) describe a regular-language lexer, so this is left null rather than stretched.

grammar-definition.comment: Token patterns live in `#[token("...")]` / `#[regex("...")]` attributes on a Rust enum processed by the `Logos` derive macro.

left-recursion.comment: Lexer only; per RESEARCH.md `n/a` for lexers.

ambiguity-handling.comment: Overlapping token patterns are resolved by longest match, then by a computed specificity priority ("Longer beats shorter. Specific beats generic."). If two patterns can match the same input with equal priority the derive macro emits a compile error, which the user resolves with `priority = N`. The listed tags are parser-oriented; `rejected-at-build` is the closest fit.

backtracking.comment: Deterministic DFA: "its matching engine will never backtrack during a token" (book). 0.16 reworked the engine to follow exact `regex` match semantics (e.g. `a*a` now matches) without runtime backtracking; unbounded greedy `.*`/`.+` are rejected at compile time unless `allow_greedy = true` because they force O(n^2) re-reads.

lexer-integration.comment: `Lexer<T>` implements `Iterator<Item = Result<T, T::Error>>`; `.spanned()` yields `(Result<T, E>, Span)` for feeding LALRPOP / chumsky.

unicode-aware.comment: "By default, logos is Unicode aware": regexes match Unicode codepoints and returned spans never split UTF-8 sequences. Byte-level matching is opt-in via `(?-u)` / byte-string patterns and `#[logos(utf8 = false)]`.

input-types.comment: `Source` is `str` by default, or `[u8]` with `#[logos(utf8 = false)]` (or when a pattern can match invalid UTF-8). The `source = ...` attribute for custom source types was removed in 0.16, so custom streams are no longer supported.

streaming-partial-input.comment: Released 0.16.1 has no partial-input API (`Lexer` docs list only `new`/`with_extras`). The master branch adds `Lexer::new_partial`, which returns `None` when more data is needed and is documented for lexing from `Read`/`AsyncRead` in chunks — unreleased as of 2026-09-19, so null per the RESEARCH.md guideline on unreleased features.

zero-copy.comment: `lex.slice()` returns a `&'source str`/`&'source [u8]` borrowed from the input; token variants can carry `&'source str` via callbacks (book example "JSON-borrowed parser").

span-tracking.comment: `Span = Range<usize>` of byte offsets via `lex.span()` / `.spanned()`. Line/column is not built in; the book shows tracking it manually in `Extras`.

output-model.comment: Produces a flat token iterator; no tree.

semantic-actions.comment: `callback = fn` on `#[token]`/`#[regex]` runs arbitrary Rust with `&mut Lexer` access (slice, span, bump, remainder, extras) and can return values, `Option`, `Result`, `Skip`, `Filter`, or `FilterResult`.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: `#[logos(skip r"[ \t\n]+")]` (optionally with callback/priority) drops trivia; alternatively emit trivia as ordinary tokens if the parser wants them.

stateful-parsing.comment: `#[logos(extras = T)]` exposes a public mutable `lex.extras` field readable/writable from callbacks; `morph()` switches to a different token enum for context-dependent (multi-mode) lexing.

error-recovery.comment: Unmatched input yields an `Err(Token::Error)` item for the unmatched slice and iteration continues with the next token (the iterator is not fused on error). No user-configurable recovery strategy beyond that.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: Each unrecognised segment is its own `Err` item in the stream, so a single pass over the input can surface many lexical errors.

expected-token-reporting.comment: Default error type is `()`; errors carry no expected-pattern set.

custom-error-types.comment: `#[logos(error = MyError)]` (must be `Default + Clone + PartialEq + Debug`, plus `From<E>` for callback errors); 0.15.1+ also allows `#[logos(error(MyError, callback = f))]` so the error constructor receives lexer context such as the span.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Every error item is paired with a byte-range `Span` via `lex.span()` / `.spanned()` (and can be baked into a custom error via the error callback), but there is no labelled secondary-span facility — 4 per the guideline.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No first-party bridge crate; the official `json` example (listed in the handbook) renders `(message, Span)` errors with `ariadne::Report`, and `ariadne` is a dev-dependency of the repo. Tagged on that documented-example basis only.

contextual-error-messages.comment: No per-pattern label/context mechanism. Callbacks and the error callback can construct richer custom errors by hand, but nothing equivalent to nom `context` or chumsky `labelled`.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Stateless single-pass lexer; no edit/reuse API.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Emits tokens only; skipped trivia is dropped unless the user chooses to emit it as tokens.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: None of the tagged editors (rust-analyzer, Helix, Zed, Neovim) depend on logos. It is used by language servers outside the tag set, e.g. Nickel (whose workspace includes `lsp-server` and `logos = "0.16"`).

runtime-speed-tier.comment: Independent benchmark (alic.dev, June 2023, Apple M1): a hand-optimised lexer beat logos by "at least 20%" (up to ~35%) in raw throughput — i.e. logos is within ~1.5x of hand-written, meeting the top-tier threshold. README reports ~1.0–1.6 GB/s on its own benchmarks. Caveat: the 0.16 engine rewrite acknowledges "a slight decrease in performance" versus 0.15; no independent post-0.16 numbers found as of 2026-09-19.

compile-time-impact.comment: The derive macro builds and optimises the DFA at compile time; issue #457 reports "up to 10 seconds" per build for a token enum using Unicode property classes (`\p{XID_Start}`), with ASCII classes as the workaround. Typical ASCII grammars are quick. `logos-cli` exists to generate the code offline (with `--check`) so the proc-macro cost is paid once.

allocation-strategy.comment: The lexer borrows the input and yields `Copy`-able tokens/spans; it compiles as `no_std` without `alloc`, so lexing itself performs no heap allocation unless callbacks do.

generated-code-size.comment: No measurements found. The derive emits one function per DFA state (tail-call style, default) or a single match-loop enum (`state_machine_codegen` feature); the book discusses speed and stack usage but not code size.

no-std-support.comment: `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]`; disable the default `std` feature. Works without `alloc`. 0.16.1 release notes fixed `no_std` issues in generated code, indicating it is exercised.

unsafe-usage.comment: By default both the runtime and the generated DFA use unchecked slice reads to skip bounds checks (validated by fuzzing). The `forbid_unsafe` feature switches to safe, bounds-checked code (~10% slower) and lets the crate be used under `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: The normal workflow is the `#[derive(Logos)]` proc-macro (`logos-derive`, on by default via `export_derive`). The `logos-cli` tool can pre-generate the same code from the annotated enum offline (`--output`, `--check`, `--format`), so the runtime crate can be used with the derive feature disabled.

build-rs-step.comment: Derive macro; no build script required (logos-cli is an optional manual/CI step, not build.rs).

dependency-count.comment: Only `logos-derive` (optional, enabled by default). The derive pulls in `logos-codegen` → fnv, proc-macro2, quote, regex-automata, regex-syntax, syn at build time.

wasm-compatible.comment: Pure Rust, `no_std`-capable runtime with no platform-specific code, so it targets wasm32 without setup. Not explicitly documented by the project; inferred from the crate's dependencies and no_std support.

async-friendly.comment: `Lexer` is `Send + Sync` (auto traits) and holds only a borrow of the input. Input must be in memory in 0.16.1; the unreleased `new_partial` API is documented for feeding from `AsyncRead` in chunks.

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads of `logos`, checked 2026-09-19 (~7.1M/month per lib.rs).

maintenance-status.comment: Release 2026-01-30; PRs merged as recently as 2026-09-11 (syn 3 upgrade, doc fixes). Day-to-day maintenance is by jeertmans (co-maintainer since the 0.13 era when the original author stepped back); 90 open issues.

documentation-quality.comment: Handbook covers attributes, disambiguation, extras, callbacks, context-dependent lexing, Unicode, unsafe, a 0.16 migration guide, debugging and six worked examples, plus solid docs.rs API docs. Several book chapters are short; not quite the depth of a full cookbook, hence 4 rather than 5.

notable-users.value: Nickel (configuration language, with LALRPOP), Fe (Ethereum language, fe-parser), chumsky (examples/dev-dependency), LALRPOP book's external-lexer tutorial
notable-users.comment: Verified via each project's Cargo.toml / docs; lib.rs counts ~2,700 dependent crates (551 direct) as of 2026-09-19.

bus-factor.comment: Original author maciejhirsz (129 commits) plus active maintainer jeertmans (217) and major contributor robot-rover (118, 0.16 engine rewrite); ~69 contributors total. Not organisation-backed.
